literal: Than the face, a more highly intelligent thing is there? Whether rejoicing or being angry, it itself will express beforehand.
translation: Is there anything more highly intelligent than the face? Whether one is pleased or angry, the face itself anticipates and expresses it first.
modern: முகத்தை விட அறிவுமிக்கது வேறு ஏதேனும் உண்டா? ஒருவன் மகிழ்ந்தாலும் அல்லது கோபித்தாலும், அவனது முகம் அவனுக்கு முன்பாகவே அதனை வெளிப்படுத்திவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet praises the face as the ultimate, instantaneous mirror of the human mind. The poet rhetorically asks if there is anything more intelligent ('முதுக்குறைந்தது') than the face. This is because whether a person feels joy ('உவப்பினும்') or anger ('காயினும்'), the face itself immediately anticipates ('முந்துறும்') and reveals those inner emotions before the person can even speak or consciously act.
